extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of English cathedral architecture, art history, and historic building practice
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative statements about the artistic, structural, and procedural qualities desirable in the design and construction of English cathedrals (medieval through thirteenth century). Emphasises aesthetic virtues, building practice, funding methods, and construction sequencing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patience in artistic construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Of all the sins of the nineteenth century, the one which most militates against its attainment of excellence in art is its impatience ... patient, finally, in its contentment to do in each age a little solidly and well, rather than a great deal indifferently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should be undertaken with long-term patience: prefer slow, careful progress and incremental, solid achievements rather than rushing to complete a large project poorly. Anti-pattern: yielding to public clamour for rapid completion at the cost of artistic quality or durability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality as natural development of style
rubrics_metrics.description: Original, not in extravagance or eccentricity, but in the realization of the natural development of style, advancing from grace to grace, from the perfection of solidity to the perfection of adornment, by an unforced growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality should arise from organic, coherent stylistic development rather than arbitrary novelty or affectation. Value designs that evolve naturally from prior work and materials, progressing toward greater refinement without forced changes. Anti-pattern: extravagance or eccentric departures that break continuity of style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity in execution and method
rubrics_metrics.description: Sincere, in its confidence of its own capacity for fulfilling its appointed end, in its grasp of the possibilities in its materials, in its choice of the true, rather than the easy, method of working.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should understand their materials and select honest, appropriate methods even when harder; choose techniques suited to function and durability rather than expedient shortcuts. Examples: workmanship that demonstrates mastery of stone and structural principles rather than merely cosmetic finishes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for artistic perfection over material completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: In its aim at artistic perfection in preference to material completeness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise achieving artistic/architectural excellence, even if it means a building remains incomplete for longer; prefer doing a smaller amount exceptionally well to completing more work to a lower standard. Example contrast: cathedrals built over long periods with careful detail vs hurried, superficially complete structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural solidity and longevity
rubrics_metrics.description: Advancing from the perfection of solidity to the perfection of adornment ... the 'jerry-building' of which rides out the storms of well-nigh seven centuries before revealing any fatal weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Durability and sound foundations are core criteria for good cathedral building. Assessments should consider long-term performance; rare structural mistakes notwithstanding, solidity that endures for centuries is a mark of success. Counter-examples: defective foundations (e.g., Peterborough central tower issues) are noted as exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of design through continuous execution
rubrics_metrics.description: None of our cathedrals are the work of one age, save those of Salisbury and London, and even they have details which they owe to succeeding times ... Salisbury ... carried out from beginning to end with unbroken unity of purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A continuous programme of building from start to finish tends to produce a coherent, unified architectural work; cathedrals comprising many epochs' additions will often be a skilled blend but can lack unity of design. Example: Salisbury is held up as an exemplar of unbroken unity; many other cathedrals are conglomerates of several orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate fundraising and patronage methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Several illustrations of the methods employed ... every man according to his degree laid his stone; some laid money ... indulgences, remitting so many days' penance, were sometimes issued to encourage the gifts of the faithful ... fines ... contributions from church dignitaries ... offerings of pilgrims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful cathedral construction historically depended on a mix of funding practices: popular gifts in kind and labour, large princely donations, ecclesiastical fines and penalties devoted to building funds, indulgences to stimulate giving, entrance fees from dignitaries, and pilgrim offerings. For planning or evaluating building projects, consider the reliability and social acceptability of funding sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction sequencing and customary building practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Salisbury Cathedral was begun in 1220, the work commencing, as was usual, at the eastern end and advancing westward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Traditional sequencing (e.g., starting at the east end and proceeding west) and established building practices affected both liturgical use and construction logistics; adherence to customary sequencing could enable partial occupation/use as parts were completed and influence stylistic cohesion.
